### AI-Research Notes (sources, blanks, and cross-language checks)

**Sources cited across this entry:**
- https://dhjhkxawhe8q4.cloudfront.net/penn-university-press/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/03/17180726/NovaReligioStyleSheet-4March-bez.doc
- https://novareligio.scholasticahq.com/for-authors

**Fields deliberately left blank, and why:**
- **positioning.accepts_now / methods_welcome / framing_required**: Could not fetch UC Press or Penn Press issue/TOC pages (403 Forbidden on online.ucpress.edu/nr/issue/27/1 and pennpress.org journal page); no 2024-2026 article title list or current CFP was retrievable within available tools. Only the generic aims-and-scope text from the Scholastica for-authors page was obtained, which is scope-level not positioning-level, so this layer is left essentially blank rather than inferred.
- **experiential.review_time_months (as experiential)**: The '~3 months' figure comes only from the journal's own stated editorial policy (Scholastica for-authors page), not from SciRev or any first-hand author report; no SciRev entry exists for this journal (scirev.org/journal/nova-religio... returned 404) and no forum thread was found, so it is not being counted as true experiential evidence.
- **experiential.desk_reject_pct**: No SciRev entry and no forum/Reddit/Chinese-forum post found reporting a desk-reject rate.
- **experiential.acceptance_note**: No first-hand acceptance/rejection narrative found on SciRev, Reddit r/AskAcademia, 小木虫 muchong.com, fabiaoji, or 知乎.
- **experiential.reviewer_culture**: No concrete first-hand source describing reviewer tone/culture found in any searched venue; per hard rule this must stay null rather than inferring from the journal's general academic reputation.
- **preprint.allowed (journal-specific confirmation)**: Direct fetch of https://www.pennpress.org/about/for-authors/reusing-your-content/ returned HTTP 403; the policy text is taken from a WebSearch AI-generated summary of that page rather than a directly verified fetch, and it is unclear if it is journal-specific vs. general Penn Press book/journal boilerplate.
